cleanIntro: The BREN 2Ms Pistol field strips without tools into the receiver with its barrel, the pistol grip with the trigger mechanism and magazine well, the rear head, the recoil assembly with its buffer, the breech block carrier assembly, the cocking handle and its guide, and the gas tube with the piston face, the piston and the piston spring. Two disassembly pins do the work: the front one holds the pistol grip, the rear one the rear head. The same procedure serves both chamberings, 5.56x45 NATO and 7.62x39. Everything below is from CZ's own CZ BREN 2Ms Pistol instruction manual.

steps.title: Magazine out — left or right release
steps.action: Point the firearm in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger. Press either the left or the right magazine release and take the magazine out of the magazine well.
steps.prose: The BREN 2Ms Pistol has a magazine release on both sides, so use whichever your hand reaches without moving the muzzle. Taking the magazine out is the first line of CZ's unloading check, not the whole of it — a round can still be in the chamber, and the next step is the one that deals with it.
steps.quote: To release the magazine from the magazine well, press the left or right magazine release (Fig. 3). Remove the magazine out of the firearm.
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Instructions for Using the Firearm — Removing the magazine, p.6
steps.warn: POINT THE FIREARM IN A SAFE DIRECTION!

steps.title: Carrier to the rear — watch the round leave the chamber
steps.action: Pull the breech block carrier fully to the rear with the cocking handle and make sure any cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected out of the firearm. Then release the breech block carrier.
steps.prose: This is the step that actually empties the gun. Watch the ejection port as the carrier comes back: a round that was chambered should come out, and you should see it leave. Pull the cocking handle smoothly all the way to the rear rather than short-stroking it, so the extractor has the full stroke to pull the case clear.
steps.quote: Pull the breech block carrier into the rear position and make sure the cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected out of the firearm;
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Instructions for Using the Firearm — Unloading the firearm (Safety check of the weapon), p.6

steps.title: Dry fire, then cycle and dry fire three times more
steps.action: With the firearm still pointed in a safe direction, pull the trigger. Then three times over, pull the breech block carrier to the rear and let it go forward, and pull the trigger each time.
steps.prose: CZ's safety check of the weapon does not stop at one look into the chamber. Cycling the carrier three more times, with a trigger pull after each, proves that nothing is feeding and nothing fires. If anything other than a click happens on any of those pulls, stop and start the unloading check again from the magazine.
steps.quote: Repeatedly (3x) pull the breech block carrier into the rear position and back and then pull the trigger
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Instructions for Using the Firearm — Unloading the firearm (Safety check of the weapon), p.6

steps.title: Selector to the white dot
steps.action: Finish the unloading check by securing the firearm: set the fire mode selector lever to the position marked with the white dot.
steps.prose: Securing the firearm is the last line of CZ's unloading check. On the BREN 2Ms Pistol the secured position is the one marked by a white dot — not a letter — so look for the dot, not an S, before you call it secured.
steps.quote: In order to secure the firearm, it is necessary to set the fire mode selector lever into the position indicated by a white dot (Fig. 4).
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Instructions for Using the Firearm — Securing the firearm, p.6

steps.title: Clean, dry mat — magazine out and unloaded
steps.action: Lay out a clean, dry mat to strip the firearm on. Before you touch the disassembly pins, confirm again that the magazine is out and the firearm is unloaded.
steps.prose: CZ sets three rules before the strip: a clean, dry mat, the magazine out and the firearm checked unloaded, and care with each part so nothing is damaged. The mat matters here because the strip produces several loose assemblies — the pistol grip, the rear head, the recoil assembly, the carrier, the gas parts — and grit picked up on any of them goes back into the action.
steps.quote: b) before disassembling the firearm, remove the magazine and check the firearm is unloaded
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping for cleaning and maintenance, p.15

steps.title: Disassembly pin out to its stop, pistol grip off
steps.action: Press the disassembly pin in from the side. Once it has moved part of the way, pull it out to its extreme position, then remove the pistol grip.
steps.prose: The pin comes out to a stop — its extreme position — rather than out of the firearm, so do not keep pulling once it stops. The pistol grip comes away with the trigger mechanism and the magazine well as one assembly; CZ's procedure does not open it.
steps.quote: 2. Depress the disassembly pin from the side and once it has partially moved, pull it out to its extreme position (Fig. 6), remove the pistol grip.
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping, step 2, p.15

steps.title: Rear disassembly pin out, rear head off downwards
steps.action: Press the rear disassembly pin in from the side until it reaches its extreme position. Push the rear head detent lever and move the rear head downwards to remove it.
steps.prose: The pistol has no folding stock to take off; its rear head comes off instead, held by a second disassembly pin. Push that pin to its stop first, then the detent lever, and the rear head comes away by moving down, not back. If it will not move, check that the pin is at its stop and the lever fully pushed before using any force.
steps.quote: 3. Depress the rear disassembly pin from the side and once it has moved to its extreme position, push the rear head detent lever and use downward movement to remove the rear head (Fig. 7).
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping, step 3, p.15

steps.title: Recoil assembly and buffer out
steps.action: With the rear head off, take out the recoil assembly together with the buffer.
steps.prose: Taking the rear head off opens the rear of the receiver, and the recoil assembly comes out as one unit with its buffer. Keep the two together and keep them on the mat; CZ gives the owner no procedure for taking the recoil assembly apart.
steps.quote: 4. Remove the recoil assembly with the buffer.
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping, step 4, p.15

steps.title: Cocking handle forward, carrier out to the rear
steps.action: Lock the cocking handle in its front position, then slide the breech block carrier assembly to the rear and out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The order matters: the cocking handle is locked forward first, and only then does the carrier slide out of the back of the receiver. The carrier comes out as an assembly with the breech block in it — CZ treats taking the carrier itself apart as a separate job.
steps.quote: 5. Lock the breech block carrier (cocking) handle in its front position and then slide the breech block carrier assembly to the rear to remove it from the receiver (Fig. 8).
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping, step 5, p.15

steps.title: Cocking handle out, then its guide
steps.action: Move the cocking handle to its rear position and take it out of the receiver. Then remove the cocking handle guide.
steps.prose: With the carrier gone, the cocking handle is free to come back to its rear position and out. The guide comes out after it. CZ notes the handle can be mounted on either side, so note which side yours came from if you want it back the same way.
steps.quote: 6. Move the breech block carrier (cocking) handle to its rear position, remove it out of the receiver and then you can remove the breech block carrier (cocking) handle guide.
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping, step 6, p.15

steps.title: Gas tube to its disassembly position and out, then the piston
steps.action: Press the gas tube detent and turn the gas tube to its disassembly position. Remove the gas tube, then remove the piston face and the piston with its piston spring.
steps.prose: The gas tube only turns past its working positions into the disassembly position while the detent is pressed. Note the position the regulator was set to before you turn it, so it goes back where you had it. The piston face, the piston and its spring come out after the tube — the gas parts are where the heaviest fouling builds up.
steps.quote: 7. Depress the gas tube detent and turn the gas tube into the disassembly position (Fig. 9). Remove the gas tube from the firearm. Subsequently, remove the piston face and the piston with the piston spring.
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping, step 7, p.15

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Receiver with barrel, pistol grip with trigger mechanism, rear head, recoil assembly with buffer, breech block carrier assembly, cocking handle and guide, gas tube, piston face, piston and piston spring. That is CZ's basic stripping for routine maintenance.
steps.prose: These parts reach everything CZ's cleaning section asks for: the bore and chamber, the gas tube and the regulator channel in the barrel, and the other parts and outer surfaces. CZ goes one level further for the owner — the breech block carrier assembly — and recommends it every 2,500 rounds or at least once a year.
steps.quote: For routine maintenance, the following procedure is sufficient for basic stripping of the firearm.
steps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Basic field stripping, p.15

deepSteps.title: When to strip the carrier — every 2,500 rounds or once a year
deepSteps.action: Strip and clean the breech block carrier assembly every 2,500 rounds, or at least once a year. You need only the universal wrench from the cleaning kit.
deepSteps.prose: This is the one deeper job CZ gives the owner, and the universal wrench in the kit is the only tool it needs. CZ's troubleshooting table also points here: a misfire with a fouled firing pin hole is cleared by cleaning that hole, and by stripping the carrier if required.
deepSteps.quote: The manufacturer recommends stripping and cleaning the breech block carrier assembly every 2500 rounds or at least once a year.
deepSteps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping the breech block carrier assembly, p.16

deepSteps.title: Firing pin plug out with the universal wrench
deepSteps.action: Remove the firing pin plug with the TORX end of the kit's universal wrench.
deepSteps.prose: The plug is the first part out. CZ's book prints the wrench as TORX X25, both here and in the cleaning kit list — it is the kit's own universal wrench. Seat it fully so the head is not damaged, and keep the plug on the mat with the carrier; it goes back last.
deepSteps.quote: remove the firing pin plug using the universal wrench TORX X25
deepSteps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Procedure for stripping the breech block carrier assembly, p.16

deepSteps.title: Move the striker block
deepSteps.action: Move the striker block, which lets the firing pin come out.
deepSteps.prose: CZ's procedure moves the striker block before the firing pin comes out; it does not take the block out. Move it only as far as it needs to go to clear the firing pin.
deepSteps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Procedure for stripping the breech block carrier assembly, p.16

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin is one of the parts CZ lists as different between the 5.56x45 NATO and 7.62x39 calibres, so keep it with this carrier and never mix it with a pin from the other calibre. Keep whatever comes out with it together on the mat.
deepSteps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Procedure for stripping the breech block carrier assembly, p.16

deepSteps.title: Operation pin out
deepSteps.prose: With the firing pin out, the operation pin is next in CZ's list, and it comes out before the breech block does. Keep it with the carrier on the mat.
deepSteps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Procedure for stripping the breech block carrier assembly, p.16

deepSteps.title: Breech block assembly out
deepSteps.action: Remove the breech block assembly from the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: The breech block comes out of the carrier as an assembly, and it stays one. This is the last item in CZ's list for the owner.
deepSteps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Procedure for stripping the breech block carrier assembly, p.16

deepSteps.title: Stop there — nothing else comes off
deepSteps.action: Do not remove any other parts. Anything that needs adjustment or repair goes to an armourer.
deepSteps.prose: CZ's caution straight after the list is the owner's stopping point: the breech block is not taken further apart, and nothing else on the carrier comes off. Clean what you have, then put the carrier back together in the reverse order you took it apart.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: Do not remove any other parts. If you believe the firearm requires adjustment or repair, entrust this work to an armourer!
deepSteps.cite: CZ BREN 2Ms PISTOL — INSTRUCTION MANUAL — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions — Stripping the breech block carrier assembly, caution, p.16

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Clean the barrel with the steel split cleaning rod and the brass bore brush; a bigger brush serves the chamber and its surroundings
Put the rod into the barrel through the muzzle, then screw the bore brush onto it
Pull the bore brush out at the muzzle
Never reverse the brush back toward the chamber — impurities always leave at the muzzle
After each pull, unscrew the brush, screw it back on and repeat
Tighten the brush thread properly — a loose thread lets the split rod come apart when it is pulled both ways
Dry the barrel with the cleaning rod loop and gauze, chamber toward muzzle, the same way
Clean the chamber and its surroundings by rotating the chamber brush inside the chamber

cleaning.name: GAS TUBE & REGULATOR CHANNEL
tasks: Clean the gas tube with a scraper and the nylon brush from the cleaning kit
With the gas tube out, look for impurities in the gas regulator channel in the barrel and in the holes of the gas tube
Clear the gas tube holes and the regulator channel with a suitable sharp object pushed through into the tube or the bore, finishing with a circular motion
Clean the bore again after cleaning the regulator channel
Darkening around the gas tube holes grows with rounds fired and is normal — it does not affect function or the life of the part

cleaning.name: OTHER PARTS & OUTER SURFACES
tasks: Dry cloth, a brush from the cleaning kit, a brass brush or a scraper on the other parts, the outer surfaces of the barrel included
Preserving oil or alcohol may also be used for cleaning
Never use a bore-cleaning agent on these parts — it can stay in the joints and cause corrosion later
Check that no cloth fibres or brush bristles are left lodged in any part

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Plastic parts of the CZ magazine: depreserve and clean with pure ethanol only
The magazine does not need lubrication to function

cleaning.name: PRESERVING
tasks: With the bore, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth dipped in gun oil
Remove any excess oil
Wipe the bore dry before shooting
The factory preservative is Ballistol; to use a different lubricant, depreserve first with petroleum benzin or ethyl alcohol, then apply the approved lubricant
Preserving vaseline (wax) is for long-term storage in severe climates only — remove it thoroughly before using the firearm

reassembly: CZ's BREN 2Ms Pistol book prints no separate reassembly sequence; this is its basic strip in reverse order, on the same clean, dry mat.

If the carrier was stripped: breech block assembly back into the carrier, then the operation pin, the firing pin, the striker block back in place, and the firing pin plug tightened with the kit's universal wrench.
Piston with its spring and the piston face back in, then the gas tube; turn it back from the disassembly position to the working position you were using.
Cocking handle guide back in, then the cocking handle.
Cocking handle locked in its front position, and the breech block carrier assembly slid back into the receiver from the rear.
Recoil assembly with its buffer back in.
Rear head back on and the rear disassembly pin pushed fully home.
Pistol grip back on and the front disassembly pin pushed fully home.
After cleaning, check that the front and rear sights are still tightened properly.
Wipe the bore dry before shooting.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty, firearm pointed in a safe direction. CZ's completeness check is a look for any damage, a check that the mechanisms and controls work correctly, and a check of the sighting before shooting. With the selector at the white dot the trigger should not fire. Work the breech block carrier fully to the rear and let it go: it should run forward cleanly. Check that the rear head is seated, that both disassembly pins are fully home, that the gas tube is in its working position, and that a magazine locks in when inserted and comes out when either release is pressed.
